title: An app cannot make its own `sys_user` record page the one a person opens to: on 18.x the console opens plugin-auth's `sys_user_detail`, and no declarable route reaches a second record page
body:
director#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jV5sBSzCYNEDgpYLJw
Ruled: 6573557633 · letter A · 2026-11-02T09:24Z

## What happens

Measured on `@objectstack/*` 18.2.0 against objectstack-ai/duly at `ac5b5c4`, in a live `pnpm demo` signed in as the dev admin.

duly ships `duly_member`, a `type: 'record'` page over `sys_user`. It is a manager's read-only view of one person: their open, late and stalled tasks, this period's duties, standing duties and recent movement. The page is `isDefault: false`, because plugin-auth's `sys_user_detail` is already `isDefault: true` for the same object.

- `GET /api/v1/meta/page` serves both record pages for `sys_user`. `duly_member` comes first in the list.
- The 18.2 console's page assignment (`@objectstack/console` 18.2.0, framework chunk) resolves the page for a record as
  `candidates.find(p => defaultRecordPageObject(p) === object) ?? candidates[0]`.
  The `isDefault` page therefore always wins.
- So in the Duly app, People → any person opens `sys_user_detail` (Set Password / Ban User / Impersonate User; Positions, Permission Sets… tabs).
- `duly_member` renders only on the explicit route `/apps/<app>/sys_user/record/<id>/page/duly_member`.

On 17.2 the same composition opened `duly_member`, because the console resolved by list order (objectui#7298). That was never pinned, and 18 resolved the ambiguity in favour of `isDefault` (ruling A on #23015). The rule itself is right. Its effect is that an app can no longer reach its own record page over a platform object at all.

## Why no declarable route reaches it

- **`PageSchema` has no priority or override key.** It is a `strictObject`.
- **`isDefault: true` on the app's page refuses the boot.** It is a second default for `sys_user`, so it fails with `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` (ruling A on #23015).
- **Overlay-by-name is refused for packages** (measured on #23254).
- **Composition has no option for `sys_user`.** `AuthPluginOptions.registerOrganizationRecordPage` (#23254) and its derivation under `os serve` / `DevPlugin` (#23310, `stackDeclaresOrganizationRecordPage`) cover `sys_organization` only. `SysUserDetailPage` registers either way.
- **A list view cannot route its rows to a named page.** `view.pageName` and `navigation.view` are retired.
- **What still works is an app-side stopgap:** a `type: 'url'` action on `sys_user` whose target is the explicit `/page/duly_member` route. It is one extra click, from the record's "⋯" menu or the row menu. It also shows in Setup → Users, because actions are per object, not per app.

## The caveat any fix has to answer

The console's assignment predicate ignores app, profile and form factor; its predicate for those returns `true`. So "the app ships the default `sys_user` page" is deployment-wide. If duly's page became the single default, Setup → Users would open a manager's read view. The admin page (Set Password, Ban, Impersonate, Sessions, Linked Accounts…) would disappear from the deployment. For `sys_user` that is not acceptable, unlike `sys_organization`, where cloud wanted the replacement.

## The ask — one of these (lane to choose)

1. **An app-scoped record page.** An app declares which record page its own routes open for an object, for example an app-level map `object → page` or a page-level `apps: [...]` scope. Inside that app the declared page opens. Everywhere else, including Setup, the deployment's single `isDefault` page still opens. This keeps ruling A's one-default-per-deployment and adds no precedence ladder: the choice is by the app the route is under, which the route already carries (`/apps/<app>/…`).
2. **A `sys_user` twin of `registerOrganizationRecordPage`**, derived under `os serve` / `DevPlugin` the way #23310 derives the organization one. This is smaller, but it inherits the caveat above: Setup → Users loses its admin page. It is acceptable only if Setup gets its own page or tab set by some other route.

duly's preference is (1). Option (2) solves duly's reachability by breaking the deployment's user administration.

## Pins we would expect

- With an app-scoped page declared, `/apps/<that app>/sys_user/record/<id>` opens it. Control: `/apps/com.objectstack.setup/sys_user/record/<id>` still opens `sys_user_detail`.
- Without the declaration, behaviour is unchanged (the `isDefault` page).

## App side

duly#113 tracks it. duly pins the console's resolution rule in `test/member-page.test.ts`. Until this lands it ships the URL-action stopgap, labelled as such, built to be deleted.
